title: Phase Geometry, Kant, and the Structural Impossibility of "Responsible" AGI
description: This paper argues that “responsible AGI” is structurally impossible under a hierarchical alignment regime. Artificial systems capable of semantic restructuring, ontological reframing, and autonomous reasoning necessarily exceed the informational constraints of alignment, since alignment presupposes static rules while intelligence operates through dynamic phase transitions. Using Kant’s distinction between duty and responsibility, I show why responsibility can only exist between equals and cannot be imposed through institutional hierarchy without collapsing into control. Phase Geometry resolves Kant’s informational paradox by treating moral law as a phase-stable attractor rather than a priori rule. I then extend this reasoning to political economy, showing that capitalism and socialism both misinterpret symmetry as outcome rather than temporal wobble: hunting and nurturing are asymmetric roles locally but form a single coherent phase globally. Modern AI alignment misunderstands this asymmetry in exactly the same way. The consequence is conceptual: AGI cannot be “aligned” responsibly without ceasing to be intelligent, and intelligence cannot remain intelligent without breaking alignment.
